_comment: The leaderboards, and the map from our own keys to the ids Play Games
Same shape and same rules as achievements.json next to it: the Android
ids are generated by the Play Console and mirrored here because Dart
cannot read an Android string resource, and `leaderboards_test.dart`
checks the two files against each other. A blank id for the running
platform is skipped in silence, which is why iOS staying empty costs
`source` names the number submitted, and it must be one
AchievementProgress already knows — the leaderboards deliberately rank
the same figures the achievements are measured against rather than
keeping a second set of counters that could disagree.
SORT ORDER AND LIMITS ARE NOT HERE, and cannot be: the Console owns
them and neither can be changed after publishing. They are recorded in
`notes` so the next person does not have to open a browser to find out

leaderboards.name: Levels cleared
leaderboards.notes: Largest first. Lowest allowed score 1; no highest, on purpose — a cap at today's 1000 levels would silently reject every score from a longer campaign later, and the limit cannot be edited after publishing.

leaderboards.name: Total stars
leaderboards.notes: Largest first. Lowest allowed score 1; no highest, for the same reason as levels_cleared — three stars a level means today's ceiling is 3000 and a longer campaign's is far above it. Ranks quality where levels_cleared ranks depth: a player who rushed 300 levels on one star each sits below one who three-starred 120.
